# T005 — Pinning and validating Node 24 LTS

## Summary

Pinned the monorepo to Node 24 LTS and verified clean installation, frontend build/type checking, lint, and offline characterization tests on Linux x86_64. Baseline Node 22.23.3/npm 10.9.9 → Node 24.21.0/npm 11.19.0.

## Changes

- `.nvmrc`: single root runtime selector (`24`); no workspace-specific selectors.
- `package.json`, `backend/package.json`, `frontend/package.json`: require Node `>=24.0.0 <25`.
- `frontend/package.json`: explicitly declare `@types/node` `^24.19.2` instead of relying on Vite's transitive Node 22 typings.
- `package-lock.json`: npm 11 regenerated workspace/typing metadata and optional platform-package entries; updated `undici-types` transitively with `@types/node`. No unrelated direct dependency version was intentionally upgraded. `backend/package-lock.json`: npm 11 updated only its root engine metadata, preserving standalone install.
- `README.md`, `backend/README.md`: update runtime prerequisites and the backend README's illustrative container base to Node 24; CI untouched.

## Decisions

- The [Node release schedule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/Release/main/schedule.json), checked 2026-10-21, identifies 24 as the newest LTS (maintenance started 2026-10-20, EOL 2028-04-30); 26 does not reach LTS until 2026-10-28. [Node 23 release notes](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v23.0.0) describe `require(esm)` becoming default; [Node 24 release notes](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.0.0) describe npm 11, V8 13.6, global `URLPattern`, test runner changes and `url.parse()` runtime deprecation. Kept application ESM and dependency families unchanged; Node 24 startup and mocked backend flows were tested instead of contacting Azure.
- Scoped engines to major 24, while `.nvmrc` selects it locally. Kept the separate backend lockfile; used npm only to regenerate both locks. npm 11 added optional architecture records and removed obsolete optional peer lock records; clean `npm ci` and the standalone backend install both succeed.
- Frontend type checking was green on Node 22 before this task (T004). Characterization suite baseline: 37 Node test-runner tests, 0 failures, 0 skips; both T003 and T005 JUnit reporters contain 36 leaf `testcase` records because the runner's parent subtest group is counted in TAP but not JUnit. No tests or validation settings changed.

## Validation

After source edits, `node -v` v24.21.0 and `npm -v` 11.19.0:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | Pass: 895 installed; four existing deprecated npm packages (`inflight`, `rimraf`, `glob`, `sudo-prompt`); npm 11 also warns that three packages' install scripts are not allowScripts-approved (`@swc/core`, `esbuild`, `keytar`). Audit: 53 findings (3 low, 12 moderate, 35 high, 3 critical). |
| `npm run build --if-present` | Pass: full TypeScript semantic check and Vite bundle; three existing CSS optimizer warnings about `display-mode`/`pointer`. |
| `npm test` | Pass: **37 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**, equal to Node 22 baseline. |
| `npm run lint --if-present` | Pass: 0 errors, five existing frontend warnings (2 exhaustive-deps, 3 react-refresh). |
| `npx tsc --noEmit -p frontend/tsconfig.json --pretty false`; `npx tsc -b --force frontend/tsconfig.json --pretty false` | Both pass, no diagnostics. |
| `npm ci --prefix backend --workspaces=false` | Pass: standalone backend install (172 packages); audit: 18 findings (6 moderate, 10 high, 2 critical). |
| `node --trace-deprecation --import tsx --test test/backend-*.test.mjs` | Pass: 19 offline backend ESM/HTTP/mock-Azure tests, including `/health`; no Node runtime deprecation trace emitted. |
| `node --import tsx --test --test-reporter=junit --test-reporter-destination=.modernization-scratch/T005-junit.xml test/*.test.mjs` | Pass: JUnit 36 leaf cases, 0 failed/skipped; same as `.modernization-scratch/T003-junit.xml`. Raw result kept outside git. |

## Follow-ups and risks

- npm deprecations, npm 11 install-script approval warnings, the 3 CSS optimizer warnings, 5 ESLint warnings, and dependency vulnerabilities remain. Security/dependency remediation is planned in subsequent tasks; warnings were not suppressed.
- Mocked offline tests cannot prove behavior against real Azure services or in a browser. No live Azure call was attempted. CI stays unchanged as explicitly requested.
